overview: The Medford City Council met to honor the crew of Ladder 2, celebrate the West Medford Community Center's 90th anniversary, and bid farewell to outgoing Vice President Kit Collins. The council also approved several municipal appropriations, labor agreements, and local ordinances, including revisions to human rights, school bus safety enforcement, overgrowth, and rodent control.

items.title: Commendation of Ladder 2 Crew
items.summary: Approved a resolution commending Lieutenant Daniel J. Marino, Firefighter Sean M. McFeely, and Firefighter Tyrell T. Patton of Ladder 2 for their heroic actions rescuing residents from a structure fire on November 7, 2025.

items.title: Celebration of West Medford Community Center
items.summary: Approved a resolution celebrating the 90th anniversary of the West Medford Community Center and honoring its role as a cornerstone of history, support, and community building.

items.title: Commendation of Vice President Kit Collins
items.summary: Approved a resolution commending Vice President Kit Collins for her outstanding, detailed, and principled service on the City Council from 2022 to 2026.

items.title: Approval of Minutes and Committee Reports
items.summary: Approved the minutes of the December 2, 2025 meeting alongside reports from the Committee of the Whole, the Resident Services and Public Engagement Committee, and the Public Health and Community Safety Committee.

items.title: Medford Standard Compensation Ordinance Amendment
items.summary: Referred a proposed standard compensation ordinance for contracted building service workers to the Committee of the Whole and requested a legal opinion from KP Law.

items.title: School Bus Safety Enforcement
items.summary: Voted to accept state legislation enabling the city to install and operate automated stop-arm camera violation monitoring systems on municipal school buses.

items.title: Reconstitution of the Human Rights Commission
items.summary: Voted to ordain a revised ordinance to revitalize and empower the city's Human Rights Commission, incorporating several amendments including a reference to the Universal Declaration of Human Rights.

items.title: McGlynn School Solar Panels PPA
items.summary: Authorized a 20-year lease and power purchase agreement with Solect Energy to install and operate solar panels at the McGlynn School.

items.title: 9-1-1 Dispatchers Union Wage Adjustment
items.summary: Approved salary schedule amendments for the 9-1-1 Dispatchers Union from 2022 through 2027.

items.title: Riverside Plaza Shade Project Contingency Funding
items.summary: Approved a Community Preservation Committee recommendation to appropriate $40,000 from the CPA Open Space Reserve for contingency needs to secure shade improvements at Riverside Plaza.

items.title: Capital Stabilization Fund Zoning Appropriation
items.summary: Approved an $85,330 appropriation from the Capital Stabilization Fund for a contract extension with zoning consultant Innes Associates.

items.title: Mystic Valley Development Commission MOU
items.summary: Authorized a memorandum of understanding with the MVDC for scheduled tax mitigation payments to the City of Malden from fiscal years 2026 through 2030.

items.title: Engineering Division Personnel Amendments
items.summary: Ordained personnel amendments establishing a new salary scale for Assistant City Engineer positions and creating a new Project Manager classification to improve recruitment.

items.title: Residential Rezoning Proposal Update
items.summary: Approved a resolution withdrawing the residential zoning amendment proposal currently with the Community Development Board and referring the council's original March draft back to committee.

items.title: Medford Square and West Medford Square Zoning Severance
items.summary: Approved a resolution legally severing Medford Square and West Medford Square zoning proposals, referring Medford Square to the Community Development Board and West Medford Square to committee.

items.title: Overgrowth Ordinance Amendment
items.summary: Ordained a new ordinance allowing the Board of Health to intervene in cases where excessive private property overgrowth creates public health or rodent hazards.

items.title: Rodent Control Ordinance Amendment
items.summary: Ordained an amendment to Chapter 6 of the municipal code to enhance the Board of Health's ability to enforce sanitation and mitigate rodent harborage on private properties.

items.title: Public Participation
items.summary: Heard comments from residents regarding federal immigration concerns, holiday greetings, and appreciation for the completed Salem Street Route 60 rotary project.
